questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: ASCII encodes A as decimal 65 and B as 66. A string 'ABBA' uses four 8-bit stored code units in this simplified example. How many bits and bytes, and why is this not proof all Unicode characters fit in one byte?
questions.answer: 4×8=32 bits=4 bytes. Unicode contains many more characters, and UTF encodings may use more than one byte for a character; 8-bit storage here is an assumption.

blocks.title: Select suitable input
blocks.text: A temperature sensor measures a physical quantity; an analogue-to-digital converter is needed if the controller uses digital samples.

blocks.title: Process and control
blocks.text: Software compares the sampled temperature with a target to decide whether to open the vent.

blocks.title: Choose appropriate outputs
blocks.text: An actuator makes the physical change; a display can show readings. Design must address accessibility and suitable latency.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: A proximity or motion sensor detects someone approaching and passes a signal to the controller.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain and check
blocks.text: A motor and driver create movement; safety sensing reduces the risk of closing onto a person.
